meta.why: Hydration supports normal health and physical function. Needs vary, so use practical cues and follow individualized medical advice when fluid intake is restricted.

hero.title: Hydration and Recovery Habits
hero.subtitle: Use practical cues instead of a rigid formula
hero.description: Hydration is one part of general health. It is not a stand-alone pain treatment, and more water is not always better. Your needs can change with activity, weather, pregnancy, illness, medications, and medical conditions.

tiles.title: **Use Everyday Cues**
content: Drink when thirsty and regularly with meals
Notice dry mouth, thirst, and unusually dark urine
Hot weather and activity may increase needs
Food and other beverages also contribute fluid

tiles.title: **Avoid One-Size-Fits-All Targets**
content: There is no single bottle count for every person
Very clear urine is not a goal you need to chase
Increase gradually around heat or longer activity
Ask for medical advice if your fluids are restricted

tiles.title: **Hydration Tips**
content: Keep water available and drink with meals
Keep water bottle visible and accessible
Adjust your routine to activity and conditions

microAction.title: Hydration Check
microAction.description: Notice your thirst, urine colour, activity, and environment. Choose one simple hydration cue, such as having a drink with each meal.
microAction.action: Choose one realistic hydration cue for today
